title: Modular Branching and the Good-Node Crystal

items.title: The cogood node gives the simple socle and head of the residue induction
items.statement:
Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\mu$ a $p$-restricted partition
of $d$ and $i\in\mathbb Z/p$ with $\varphi_i(\mu)>0$; let $B$ be the cogood
$i$-node and $\nu=\mu\cup B$
([[def-residue-signature-normal-good-conormal-and-cogood-nodes]]). Then
$F_iD(\mu)$ has simple socle and simple head, both isomorphic to $D(\nu)$,
and the total (ungraded) multiplicity of $D(\nu)$ in $F_iD(\mu)$ is
$\varphi_i(\mu)$
([[def-generalized-jm-primary-idempotents-and-residue-summand-functors]]).
items.strategy: The proof uses the recorded dual source statement (Kleshchev survey §11.4 with Theorem 11.7; Brundan §5.5) for the simple socle and head, and computes the total multiplicity $\varphi_i(\mu)$ locally from the conormal-node theorem applied to the cogood node $B$, which is the bottommost conormal node. The endpoint identification is completed by antipode-invariance of the residue idempotents and self-duality of the simple modules (head = dual of socle), and the characteristic-$2$ calibration $p=2$, $\mu=(1)$ checks $F_1D(1)\cong kS_2$ with socle, head and total multiplicity $2$ $= \varphi_1(1)$. The proof does not use any unshifted duality of $F_i$ and $E_i$.
